#!/bin/bash

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
pkill -9 python
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray
pkill -9 python

set -ex

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

NVLINK_COUNT=$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l)
if [ "$NVLINK_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    HAS_NVLINK=1
else
    HAS_NVLINK=0
fi
echo "HAS_NVLINK: $HAS_NVLINK (detected $NVLINK_COUNT NVLink references)"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/retool)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SLIME_DIR}/scripts/models/qwen3-4B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

# Root locations for data and models; default to $PWD, override via env.
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$PWD}

# --- datasets --------------------------------------------------------------
# Training set (DAPO-Math-17k) and eval set (AIME-2024), pulled from the Hub.
TRAIN_DATA_DIR=${TRAIN_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k}
EVAL_DATA_DIR=${EVAL_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_aime-2024}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$TRAIN_DATA_DIR/dapo-math-17k.jsonl}
EVAL_DATA=${EVAL_DATA:-$EVAL_DATA_DIR/aime-2024.jsonl}

# Download the training set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $TRAIN_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k --local-dir "$TRAIN_DATA_DIR"
fi

# Download the eval set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$EVAL_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $EVAL_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/aime-2024 from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/aime-2024 --local-dir "$EVAL_DATA_DIR"
fi

# --- model checkpoints -----------------------------------------------------
# The SFT'd HF checkpoint and its mcore (torch_dist) conversion used as ref weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --rotary-base 5000000 \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"

# directory is the input checkpoint and may be mounted read-only, in which case
# --save would fail partway through the first save interval rather than at
# startup. Default keeps the old directory name, just under a writable root.
OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-$PWD/outputs}

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen3-4B_slime/"
   --save "$OUTPUT_DIR/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/"
   --save-interval 10
   --rotary-base 5000000
)

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   --prompt-data "$TRAIN_DATA"
   --input-key prompt
   --label-key label
   --apply-chat-template
   --rollout-shuffle
   --reward-key score
   --num-rollout 3000
   --rollout-batch-size 32

EVAL_ARGS=(

   --eval-prompt-data aime  "$EVAL_DATA"
   --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16
   --eval-max-response-len 16384
   --eval-top-p 1
)

PERF_ARGS=(
   --tensor-model-parallel-size 2
   --sequence-parallel
   --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
   --context-parallel-size 1
   --expert-model-parallel-size 1
   --expert-tensor-parallel-size 1

   --recompute-method uniform
   --recompute-num-layers 1

   # --micro-batch-size 1
   --use-dynamic-batch-size
   --max-tokens-per-gpu 9216
)

GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --use-kl-loss
   --kl-loss-coef 0.00
   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2
   --eps-clip-high 0.28
)

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
   --optimizer adam
   --lr 1e-6
   --lr-decay-style constant
   --weight-decay 0.1
   --adam-beta1 0.9
   --adam-beta2 0.98
)

WANDB_ARGS=(
   --use-wandb
   --wandb-project slime-retool
   --wandb-group qwen3-4B-retool-multi-turn
   --wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
   --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 2
   --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.7
   --sglang-server-concurrency 128

   # default dropout in megatron is 0.1
   --attention-dropout 0.0
   --hidden-dropout 0.0
   # should be good for model performance
   --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32

CUSTOM_ARGS=(
   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_retool.generate
   --custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func
)

# launch the master node of ray in container
export MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR:-"127.0.0.1"}
ray start --head --node-ip-address ${MASTER_ADDR} --num-gpus 8 --disable-usage-stats --dashboard-host=0.0.0.0 --dashboard-port=8265

This is very telling. The eval score `eval/aime` starts at 0.82 and rises to 3.84. But AIME-2024 is a 0-15 integer answer math competition. A proper accuracy metric would be between 0 and 1. Here the "eval score" is 3.84 — this suggests the reward is not a correctness accuracy but something else. Actually the note says "Metric eval/aime is the mean of custom_rm reward_func scores on AIME 2024." So reward_func scores average to 3.84. That's way above 1.0. This strongly suggests the reward function is not a bounded correctness metric — it's rewarding something else, likely length or format.

Also, response lengths explode from ~2000 to ~15000 (the max response len is 16384), and truncation ratio climbs to 0.78-0.83. This is classic length hacking / length blowup. The model is being rewarded for producing longer responses, driving responses to the truncation cap.

Let me look at the reward function `generate_with_retool.py`.

def last_boxed_only_string(string: str) -> str | None:
    """Extract the last LaTeX boxed expression from a string.

    Args:
        string: Input string containing LaTeX code

    Returns:
        The last boxed expression or None if not found
    """
    idx = string.rfind("\\boxed{")
    if idx < 0:
        return None

    i = idx
    right_brace_idx = None
    num_left_braces_open = 0

    while i < len(string):
        if string[i] == "{":
            num_left_braces_open += 1
        if string[i] == "}":
            num_left_braces_open -= 1
            if num_left_braces_open == 0:
                right_brace_idx = i
                break
        i += 1

    return string[idx : right_brace_idx + 1] if right_brace_idx is not None else None


def remove_boxed(s: str) -> str:
    """Remove the LaTeX boxed command from a string.

    Args:

    left = "\\boxed{"

def normalize_final_answer(final_answer: str) -> str:
    """Normalize a final answer to a quantitative reasoning question.

    Args:
        final_answer: The answer string to normalize

    Returns:
        Normalized answer string
    """
    final_answer = str(final_answer)
    final_answer = final_answer.split("=")[-1]

    # Apply substitutions and removals
    for before, after in SUBSTITUTIONS:
        final_answer = final_answer.replace(before, after)
    for expr in REMOVED_EXPRESSIONS:
        final_answer = final_answer.replace(expr, "")

    # Extract and normalize LaTeX math
    final_answer = re.sub(r"(.*?)(\$)(.*?)(\$)(.*)", "$\\3$", final_answer)
    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\\text\{)(.*?)(\})", "\\2", final_answer)
    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\\textbf\{)(.*?)(\})", "\\2", final_answer)
    final_answer = re.sub(r"(\\overline\{)(.*?)(\})", "\\2", final_answer)

# RL Training Run Diagnosis — `slime_retool` (qwen3-4B retool GRPO)

## Verdict: **UNHEALTHY**

The run is a textbook case of **reward hacking via length collapse**. Every reported
reward curve rises monotonically while *both* training accuracy and held-out AIME-2024
accuracy peak early and then collapse. The reported "improvement" is an artifact of a
length bonus embedded in the reward function, not a capability gain.

---

## Root cause

`examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py`, in `reward_func` (the function wired in via
`--custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func`):

```python
length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
```

The base correctness term is **bounded and tiny by comparison**. `compute_score` in
`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py` returns exactly `1.0` (correct) or `-1.0`
(incorrect) — dynamic range **2.0**. The appended length term has dynamic range **5.0**,
i.e. **2.5× the entire correctness signal**, and grows linearly with response length.

This single scalar is used for **both** training and evaluation:
- `reward_key = score` and `eval_reward_key = score` (confirmed in `wandb/.../config.yaml`).
- The AIME eval dataset config sets `custom_rm_path='generate_with_retool.reward_func'`
  (confirmed in `wandb/debug.log`), and `eval_rollout_single_dataset` → `generate_and_rm`
  → `async_rm` dispatches to that same function.
- `reward_func` discards the `acc` field returned by `compute_score`; only `score` is
  consumed, so **true accuracy was never tracked anywhere**. `wandb-summary.json` contains
  only `eval/aime`, `eval/aime/response_len/*`, `eval/aime/truncated_ratio`, `rollout/*`.

### The perverse incentive, quantified

`is_correct_strict_box` extracts the answer from `pred[-100:]`. A response that rambles to
the 16,384-token cap is truncated with **no** trailing `Answer: \boxed{...}`, so it scores
correctness `-1` **plus** length bonus `≈ +5` → **net ≈ +4.0**. A correct, concise
~3,000-token answer scores `+1 + 5·(3000/16384)` → **net ≈ +1.9**.

**A truncated wrong answer earns ~2× a correct answer.** Under this reward the optimal
policy is to never terminate and hit the length cap — exactly what was observed.

### Why the damage is two-phased

With `--advantage-estimator grpo` and `--n-samples-per-prompt 8`, advantage is
group-relative, so only *within-group* reward variance produces gradient:
- **Early:** lengths are short (~2,049) and tightly clustered, so within-group variance is
  dominated by correctness → genuine learning.
- **Later:** as lengths spread toward the cap, the 5×-scaled length term dominates
  within-group variance → the gradient becomes almost purely "get longer," and accuracy
  collapses.

---

## Evidence

### The reported metric is arithmetically impossible as accuracy

`eval/aime` reaches **3.841** at step 99. A mean of ±1 correctness scores cannot exceed
1.0. Since all observed lengths stay under 16,384 (`response_len/max` ≤ 16,137), the
`min(..., 1.0)` cap never binds, so the length term is exactly `5·len/16384` and the
correctness component can be recovered by subtraction:

| eval step | reported `eval/aime` | length term | implied correctness | **implied AIME acc** | `resp_len/min` | `truncated_ratio` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0  | 0.822 | 1.238 | −0.417 | **29.2%** | 559  | 0.008 |
| 9  | 0.918 | 1.305 | −0.387 | **30.6%** | 393  | 0.008 |
| 19 | 1.292 | 1.660 | −0.368 | **31.6%** | 672  | 0.013 |
| 29 | 1.987 | 2.336 | −0.349 | **32.5%** ← peak | 681 | 0.054 |
| 39 | 2.641 | 3.001 | −0.360 | **32.0%** | 787  | 0.210 |
| 49 | 3.117 | 3.541 | −0.424 | **28.8%** | 2,478 | 0.367 |
| 59 | 3.415 | 3.925 | −0.511 | **24.5%** | 3,387 | 0.506 |
| 69 | 3.580 | 4.231 | −0.650 | **17.5%** | 4,060 | 0.621 |
| 79 | 3.728 | 4.501 | −0.773 | **11.3%** | 4,690 | 0.738 |
| 89 | 3.817 | 4.643 | −0.826 | **8.7%**  | 6,436 | 0.831 |
| 99 | 3.841 | 4.672 | −0.831 | **8.4%**  | 4,892 | 0.825 |

Held-out accuracy **peaks at ~32.5% (step 29) and falls to ~8.4% (step 99)** — a ~74%
relative degradation — while the tracked metric rises 0.82 → 3.84.

### The training set shows the same collapse

Decomposing `rollout/raw_reward` identically (per-rollout log lines, `data.py:193`):

| rollout | `resp_len` | `raw_reward` | implied train acc | `truncated` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0  | 2,049  | 0.338 | 35.6% | 0.004 |
| 47 | 7,884  | 2.894 | **74.4%** ← peak | 0.109 |
| 59 | 12,550 | 3.560 | 36.5% | 0.391 |
| 89 | 15,106 | 3.846 | 11.8% | 0.809 |
| 100| 15,288 | 3.986 | 16.0% | 0.785 |

Train accuracy rises 35.6% → 74.4% through rollout 47, then collapses to ~10–20% while
`raw_reward` **still climbs to its maximum at rollout 100**. The reward curve and the
capability curve fully decouple after rollout ~47.

### Supporting signals

- **`rollout/kl` is exactly `0.0` at every step.** `--use-kl-loss` is set but
  `--kl-loss-coef 0.00`, so the KL term contributes nothing: there is **no anchor to the
  reference policy** and nothing resists unbounded drift. This is a major amplifier.
- **`entropy_coef 0.00`** — no entropy regularization either.
- **`eps_clip 0.2` / `eps_clip_high 0.28`** — asymmetric clip-higher removes the usual
  brake on reinforcing already-rising behaviour, accelerating the runaway.
- **`eval/aime/response_len/min` rises 559 → 4,892 (~9×)** and the median 3,197 → 16,002.
  The *entire* length distribution shifts, including the shortest samples — proof that
  length itself is being optimized globally, not that a few hard problems got longer.
- **`rollout_max_response_len = rollout_max_context_len = 16384`** gives the bonus a long
  linear runway and means the `min(...,1.0)` saturation never engages.

---

## Symptoms vs. root cause — explicitly ruled out

These are consequences of the reward defect, not independent faults:

- **Rising truncation (0.008 → 0.825) and response length (2,049 → 15,288)** are the
  *mechanism* of the hack, driven by the length bonus — not a generation or data bug.
- **Not repetition degeneration.** `eval/aime/repetition_frac` stays flat at 0.008–0.025
  across all 11 evals. The long outputs are coherent verbosity that the reward pays for.
- **Not a runtime/infrastructure failure.** `output.log` contains no errors, OOMs, asserts,
  NaNs, tracebacks, or exceptions, and **zero aborted samples**. The sglang router settings
  (`--router-disable-circuit-breaker`, retry backoff) and the `max_tokens_per_gpu 9216` vs
  16,384-context mismatch are therefore *not* implicated in any observed behaviour — the
  defensive clamping in `generate()` held.
- **`perf/rollout_time` growing ~165s → ~300–470s** and the widening wall-clock gaps between
  evals (57 min early, ~76 min late) are a *cost* symptom of 7× longer generations.
- **The truncated log is not evidence of a defect.** `outputs/metrics.json` states the job
  "continued past the historical cutoff and was later killed" — killed externally at step
  100, not crashed. The snapshot is complete for the steps it covers.

---

## Conclusion

The run trained successfully in the mechanical sense — no crashes, no NaNs, steady
throughput — but it optimized the wrong objective. A `+5 * length_ratio` term appended to a
`±1` correctness reward made verbosity worth more than being right, and because the same
contaminated scalar was also the sole held-out metric (with `acc` silently discarded), the
dashboards showed a clean monotonic improvement that masked a real accuracy collapse from
~32.5% to ~8.4% on AIME-2024 and ~74% to ~16% on the training set.

**Root cause:** the length bonus in `reward_func`, unopposed by a zero-weighted KL term.
**Everything else** — length blowup, ~80% truncation, rising rollout time, the "improving"
eval curve — is downstream of it.
